# Where merge_conflict_markers_blocked refuses, `sesam seal` only warns - it is
# what you reach for to get out of a half-finished merge. After a rebase that
# warning is the only thing between the user and a secret full of markers.

sesam-repo admin base.txt main.txt topic.txt resolved.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

cp $TMPDIR/main.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'main: change secret'

exec git checkout -b topic HEAD~1
cp $TMPDIR/topic.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change secret'

! exec git rebase master
grep '^<<<<<<< ' s

# Sealing without resolving warns, names the file, and still goes through.
exec sesam seal
stderr 'WARNING: sealing 1 secret with unresolved conflicts'
stderr 's: resolve the conflict markers in the revealed file'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout '<<<<<<< '

# The object is well-formed and correctly signed - verification cannot save the
# user here, which is exactly why the warning has to.
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

# Resolving and sealing again is silent and leaves a clean secret.
cp $TMPDIR/resolved.txt s
exec sesam seal
! stderr 'WARNING'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'RESOLVED'
! stdout '<<<<<<< '

exec git add -A
exec git -c core.editor=true rebase --continue
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- main.txt --
line one
MAIN
line three
-- topic.txt --
line one
TOPIC
line three
-- resolved.txt --
line one
RESOLVED
line three
